parts.text: Which claim correctly explains the pattern by rewriting the terms?

options.text: Each sum is $2(1+2+\cdots+n)=n(n+1)$, so the totals are $2\cdot 3$, $3\cdot 4$, and $4\cdot 5$.
Odd numbers is the label that belongs on these even sums.
The pattern is settled by translating a heads-and-legs puzzle into equations.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Reyansh looks at the even sums $2+4$, then $2+4+6$, then $2+4+6+8$.

part_answers.answer: Factor out $2$ to get twice a triangular sum of the first $n$ positives, which equals $n(n+1)$.

teacher.key_rationale: Rewriting 2+4+...+2n as 2(1+...+n)=n(n+1) explains all listed sums at once.
